public_rationale: The central relationship claim is documented: Microsoft had cloud exclusivity with OpenAI and also distributed Mistral's models. The full statement includes an unresolved financial premise. Contemporary reporting used both $11 billion and $13 billion, without establishing a comparable measure of funding already provided. Marcus identifies no financial basis in the supplied passage. Under the required money-claim rules, these figures cannot establish or refute the complete claim. Cloud exclusivity also does not by itself prove a broader exclusivity demand.
limitations: The unresolved verdict concerns the compound claim; it does not cast doubt on the documented Mistral partnership.
News reporting supplies the numerical context because the retrieved primary disclosures do not settle the stated amount.
No inference of contractual breach or improper conduct is made.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft put $11 billion in (the post says 'into Microsoft', apparently a typo for OpenAI) and demanded an exclusive from OpenAI, yet Microsoft itself is 'seeing other people', that is, working with other AI partners.
conditions: despite having put $11 billion in and demanded an exclusive from OpenAI

statement.excerpt: You might think that after Microsoft put $11 Billion into Microsoft and demanded an exclusive from OpenAI, that Microsoft wouldn’t “see other people”, but they are.
statement.document_title: Microsoft and OpenAI’s increasingly complicated relationship

from_speaker: Microsoft wouldn’t “see other people”, but they are
our_interpretation: I read the second occurrence of Microsoft as a typo for OpenAI.
The ordinary reading is that Microsoft had invested $11 billion in OpenAI, secured exclusivity from it, and nevertheless worked with other AI developers.
I interpret exclusivity as cloud-provider exclusivity. The wording does not specify its scope or establish that Microsoft required exclusivity across every commercial relationship.
I interpret seeing other people as commercial collaboration with another AI developer, including distributing its models.

The target is the cumulative history leading to the relationship described on May 6, 2024. The starting date is unspecified. These investments and agreements are discrete events, so a quarterly reporting window would be inappropriate.

The supplied passage identifies no source or accounting basis for $11 billion. Its financial basis is therefore unknown. I do not silently substitute commitments for funding already provided, or treat $11 billion as a $11–13 billion range.
Despite introduces historical premises, not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes the stated cumulative investment on an identifiable financial basis, OpenAI's applicable exclusivity obligation, and Microsoft's collaboration with another AI developer by May 6, 2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes a materially different investment amount on the same basis, or directly disproves the claimed exclusivity or other-partner relationship. A different commitment total alone does not disprove an amount already funded.

evidence.explanation: Microsoft describes an exclusive cloud-provider relationship. This supports the narrower contractual reading, but does not establish a blanket ban on OpenAI working with other companies or document a specific negotiating demand.
The $11 billion figure appeared in contemporary reporting. This is contextual corroboration, because the report does not reconcile funding, commitments, or the later total.

This pre-post report gives a different investment total. It is material counterevidence to an exact $11 billion reading, but does not distinguish commitments from funding provided and therefore cannot decisively contradict that measure.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An identifiable basis for Marcus's figure and records reconciling cumulative funding, computing credits, and outstanding commitments by May 6, 2024; contractual or negotiation records would settle any stronger reading of demanded exclusivity.
